context: Stock dashboard data visualization — sortable table with four embedded sparkline types per row: area price trend, volume bars, win/loss streak, and bullet chart for performance vs target
first_impression: Polished and information-dense, with deliberate typographic hierarchy and a clearly chosen palette that reads as designed rather than default
what_works: Paul Tol bright palette for sector badges is a non-default, accessible choice that gives the badges clear semantic weight; typographic hierarchy is genuinely layered — uppercase tracked headers, bold monospace tickers, muted gray company names, and tabular-nums for prices all working together
what_doesnt: Price sparklines share a single global domain across all 25 stocks, so a stock at $30 and one at $490 both render nearly flat, draining the trend encoding of meaning; bullet chart qualitative range bands (three barely-distinguishable grays) are invisible at the rendered size and add no perceptual value
